description: "Use on first run with a new owner: onboard them one question at a time, list what they provide, and run the first Streamer Scout, Patch Notes & Update Hype Director grade with the lens engine."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-20-streamer-hype-director v1.4.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Streamer Scout, Patch Notes & Update Hype Director: Getting Started

Match creators to your intended audience and turn verified build changes into patch notes and updates for players.

This template fits any game. Spectator, streamer-mode and season features apply only if your game has them. "Update Hype" in the name means the build-up to each update, or to each season when your game runs them.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `streamer-hype-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. Start every profile value from `fixtures/good-pack.json` and ask the owner to confirm or replace it; the sample values are synthetic examples, never defaults.

1. Which game are we working on? Then ask, one at a time: which build should we check (a build id or commit), and what produces the evidence pack (a CI job or a manual capture)?
2. How do you update the game: one release with occasional patches, regular updates, or seasons? This sets the rhythm for patch notes. Season wording is used only if you run seasons.
3. Does your game record replays or clips, or offer a streamer mode? If it has no streamer mode and never shows player names, chat or account details on screen, we use the `no-streamer-mode` profile: `creator-controls:1` reads N/A, `creator-controls:2` takes its points and the redaction blockers no longer apply.
4. Does your game have a spectator mode, a live watch view or a public feed of live play? If not, we use the `no-spectator-mode` profile: the spectator lines read N/A, their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines, and the spectator release blockers no longer apply.
5. Does your game create share or watch links? If not, we use the `no-share-links` profile: `creator-controls:2` reads N/A and `creator-controls:1` takes the pillar's 20 points.
6. How much frame time may recording add on each device? This sets `maxCaptureOverheadMs`.
7. At which resolutions do creators stream or record your game? This sets `streamResolutions`.
8. Only if your game has share links: what tag should every link carry, so you can tell where visits come from? This sets `shareTag`.
9. Only if your game has a spectator or streaming mode: what may a spectator see, and how long must a feed lag behind live play? This sets the information policy and `minStreamDelayMs`.
10. Which creators or communities already play games like yours? These are starting points for the shortlist.
11. Who reviews the local drafts: patch notes, outreach messages and findings?

Read the profiles you picked back to the owner and, once they approve, set them before scoring, for example `"rubricProfile": ["no-spectator-mode"]` in `pack.profile`. An N/A line is not U and not a defect, and the verdict can reach PASS.

Before grading a real pack, match its build and profile to what the owner approved. Record unavailable capture or execution as NOT_RUN. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` to see the population each line needs (the list or count of things measured, such as share links or patch note lines).

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Metric groups this engine reads: `recording` (capture), `captureCost` (trace), `spectatorPolicy` (capture), `spectatorRead` (capture), `streamerMode` (capture), `links` (trace), `notes` (static), `claims` (static), `fairness` (trace), `receipts` (static), `spectatorLinks` (capture).
- Profile thresholds in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Receipts: one result row per test case agreed in `profile.cases`, with the measured values. For example, one `shippedClaims` row per patch note line with its commit and whether its feature switch is on in the shipped build.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect. A feature your game does not have (for example a spectator mode) also stays out of the pack; when an approved profile covers it, its lines read N/A instead of U.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade) and `tickets` (deduplicated candidates).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- Name the rubric profiles used next to the grade. List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them, or "does not apply" when the game lacks the feature. Never call U or N/A lines defects.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines: capture-reliability:1, capture-reliability:2, spectator-comprehension:1, spectator-comprehension:2, creator-controls:1, creator-controls:2, truthful-claims:1, truthful-claims:2, player-safety:1, player-safety:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `git-diff-patch-notes-hype-compiler`: patch notes where every line maps to a commit and every claim matches the shipped build. Fills `notes` and `claims` (truthful-claims:1 and 2).
- `stream-and-replay-features-review`: recording, capture cost, streamer mode, share links, fairness and, if your game has one, the spectator view and stream delay. Fills `recording`, `captureCost`, `streamerMode`, `links`, `fairness`, `receipts`, and for spectator games `spectatorPolicy`, `spectatorRead` and `spectatorLinks`.
- `creator-shortlist-scout`: a creator shortlist with dated sources and outreach drafts for the owner. Fills `creatorLog` (a growth check, not scored).
- `streamer-hype-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Recording checks need a real capture of your build; nothing is published by the agent.
- If your game has a spectator or streaming mode, a measured stream delay or spectator information failure blocks release. If your game has a streamer mode or shows names, an exposed name or sensitive detail in a capture blocks release; without either, the `no-streamer-mode` profile switches those blockers off.

Use the same scene and build for paired capture-on and capture-off runs. Reopen the export and, if your game has spectators, compare spectator views to the approved information and delay policy.

Before capture, agree on the case IDs and expected values in `profile.cases`. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact ID. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

skills.description: Use when shortlisting streamers and creators to contact: fit with the game, audience, safety and a clear reason, without inventing audience numbers, with outreach kept as local drafts.

name: creator-shortlist-scout
description: "Use when shortlisting streamers and creators to contact: fit with the game, audience, safety and a clear reason, without inventing audience numbers, with outreach kept as local drafts."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-20-streamer-hype-director v1.4.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.

> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Creator shortlist

Find creators whose viewers would enjoy your game, record why, and draft outreach for the owner to send. This works the same for a single-player game, a co-op game or a competitive one.

## Method
1. Fit: the creator already plays games like yours, on the platforms you support. Note two recent videos or streams as evidence. Examples of fit:
   - Single-player narrative or horror game: creators who play story games start to finish with commentary.
   - Farming or life sim: creators with long, relaxed sessions and returning viewers.
   - Turn-based strategy game: creators who run long campaign series and explain their moves.
   - Mobile puzzle game: short-video creators who post daily puzzle clips.
   - Racing game: creators who post time trials or car setups.
   - Competitive multiplayer game: creators who already stream the genre with friends or viewers.
2. Audience: record numbers only from a source you opened this run, with the date. Save the source link locally. If access fails, mark the check NOT_RUN and leave the number blank.
3. Safety: check recent content against your brand and age rules.
4. Reason: one sentence on why this creator and what you would offer, for example a key, early access to an update, or the press kit from template 19.
5. Outreach: draft one short, honest message per creator for the owner to approve and send. Never contact anyone automatically. If the offer is paid or includes a free key, the draft asks the creator to disclose it as their platform requires.
6. Keep a local source log per shortlist decision with the observation date, two source references, the review role and the reason. Leave inaccessible numbers blank and mark the observation NOT_RUN.

## Example outreach draft (synthetic)
"Hi <creator name>, I make <game name>, a single-player <genre> about <one line>. Your <series name> series is why I am writing: <one specific reason>. I would like to offer you a key and our press kit (<link>). No deadline and no obligation. If you play it on stream, please mention that the key was free."

The owner edits and sends it. The agent never sends.

## What this fills in the pack
- `creatorLog` for the `creator-sources` growth check: one entry per shortlist decision with `observedOn`, `sourceRef`, `reason`, `sourceOpened` and `reviewed`. The creator log supports the draft shortlist and earns no grade points.

## Pitfalls
- Follower counts are not reach; prefer recent average views when they are visible.
- Ranking by size alone; a small creator who plays your genre often reaches more of the right players.

## Negative fixture
Add a creator with no opened source for their numbers and confirm the shortlist check marks the entry unmeasured.

## Worked example (synthetic)
Synthetic example, single-player puzzle adventure: 12 candidates found; 7 have two recent videos of story or puzzle games; numbers were visible for 5 (opened this run, dated); 1 fails the brand check. Report: shortlist of 6 with reasons, 1 dropped for safety, numbers marked unmeasured where not visible, outreach drafts waiting for the owner.

Tell the owner what the shortlist covers and what stays unmeasured.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `streamer-hype-lens-engine`).

skills.name: git-diff-patch-notes-hype-compiler
skills.description: Use when writing patch notes from commits: every line maps to a commit, and every claim matches the code that shipped.
skills.content:
---
name: git-diff-patch-notes-hype-compiler
description: "Use when writing patch notes from commits: every line maps to a commit, and every claim matches the code that shipped."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-20-streamer-hype-director v1.4.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Patch notes from commits

Turn the changes between two releases into player-facing notes where every line is true on the build players get.

## Method
1. List the changes between the last release and the shipped commit (for example `git log <last-release-tag>..<shipped-sha>`), or start from a verified change list if your team keeps one.
2. Write one player-facing line per change that matters; each line names its commit (`notes.lines`, `notes.mappedToCommits`). Record one `receipts.shippedClaims` row per line with the claim, the commit, whether its feature switch is on in the shipped build, and a capture from that build.
3. Claims check: for each claim (numbers, new features, fixes, technical promises such as crash recovery or faster loading), confirm the code matches (`claims.claims`, `claims.matchingCode`).
4. Group by what players notice first: fixes to bugs they reported, then balance or tuning, then new content.
5. Never claim a fix that has not been verified on the live build. A feature behind a switch that is off stays out of the notes.
6. Fit the notes to how your game is updated:
   - One release with occasional patches (most single-player games): a short, version-numbered note per patch.
   - Regular updates, or seasons if your game runs them: a headline note per update, with the same commit mapping for every line.
   - Mobile store releases: a very short "what's new" text that fits the store's field, with the longer note on your own site.

## Examples (synthetic)
- Single-player narrative adventure, patch 1.0.2: "Fixed a save that would not load after chapter 3." "Added a subtitle size option." "Puzzle hints in chapter 5 now appear after 3 failed tries instead of 5."
- Mobile puzzle game: "Levels 41 to 60 are here." "Fixed the board not rotating on some tablets."
- Racing game: "Night tracks are brighter on low graphics settings."
- Online game with seasons (only if your game runs them): "Season 3 adds two new maps, and the ranked ladder resets."

## Pitfalls
- Writing notes from commit titles without checking the shipped build.
- Promising features that are behind a switch or not live yet.

## Negative fixture
Add an internal-only commit (a refactor or a secret rename) to a test range and confirm it does not reach player-facing notes. Mark one claimed feature's switch as off and confirm truthful-claims:1 drops to 0.

## Worked example (synthetic)
Synthetic example: 41 commits in the range; 9 player-facing changes confirmed in the shipped build; 3 internal refactors and 1 switched-off feature left out. Report: notes for 9 changes, each linked to its commit and checked in the build, plus the list of what was left out and why.

The notes stay a local draft; only the human posts them.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `streamer-hype-lens-engine`).

skills.description: Use when your game has recording, replays, a streamer mode, share links or a spectator view: check each works, hides private information, keeps any required stream delay and cannot change results.

---
name: stream-and-replay-features-review
description: "Use when your game has recording, replays, a streamer mode, share links or a spectator view: check each works, hides private information, keeps any required stream delay and cannot change results."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-20-streamer-hype-director v1.4.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Review stream, replay and spectator features

Check the features that creators and viewers touch. Each part applies only if your game has that feature; skip the rest. A missing spectator mode or share links has an approved profile (its lines read N/A); any other missing part leaves its lines unmeasured.

## Which parts apply

| If your game has | Check | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Recording, replays or clip export | It replays and exports with correct sound and credit, and recording costs little frame time | capture-reliability:1 and 2 |
| A spectator mode, a live watch view or a public feed | Viewers see only what the policy allows, after the required delay, and the view reads at stream resolutions | spectator-comprehension:1 and 2, the `spectator-links` check (if none: `no-spectator-mode` profile) |
| A streamer mode, or names and chat on screen | Names and sensitive details are hidden in captures | creator-controls:1 (if none: `no-streamer-mode` profile) |
| Share links | Each link carries your source tag and opens | creator-controls:2 (if none: `no-share-links` profile) |
| Viewer or creator features (votes, chat commands, rewards for watching) | They cannot change results, saves or rankings | player-safety:1 |

A single-player game with no spectator mode usually still has recording or share links, and may have a streamer mode (hiding the player's account name or swapping licensed music). With the owner's approval before scoring, set `"rubricProfile": ["no-spectator-mode"]` in the game profile and leave the spectator groups out of the pack. The spectator lines then read N/A, never U and never a defect, their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines, the spectator release blockers no longer apply, and the verdict can reach PASS. Say in the report which profiles were used.

## Method
1. Recording and replay: record one complete session, replay it and export it. Check the sound, the attribution (the game name and creator credit, where shown) and that the file opens (`recording`).
2. Capture cost: run the same replay or scene on the same build and device twice, capture off then on. Compare p95 frame time (the time that 95 percent of frames stay under) against `maxCaptureOverheadMs` (`captureCost`, `receipts.capturePairs`).
3. Spectator view, if your game has one: define when a viewer can enter, switch and leave watch mode. In a turn-based game a player may watch other players' turns. In a co-op game a downed player may watch until revived. In a racing game a finished driver may watch the rest of the field. In a competitive game an eliminated player may watch the rest of the match. Record which viewpoints and information a viewer may see.
4. Spectator policy and stream delay, if your game has a spectator or streaming mode: inspect every feed a viewer can open (a public view, a partner feed, a tournament feed) under the approved information policy. Record the observed delay and any restricted fields shown (`spectatorPolicy`, `receipts.partnerFeeds`, `spectatorLinks`). The delay must be at least `minStreamDelayMs`, so a viewer cannot pass live hidden information to a player. A measured delay or disclosure failure blocks release.
5. Readability: watch the spectator view at every resolution in `streamResolutions` (`spectatorRead`).
6. Streamer mode: capture a session with streamer mode on and look for player names, account details, chat, friend lists and other sensitive information (`streamerMode`). Any leak blocks release.
7. Share links: open every share link and confirm it carries the `shareTag` and resolves (`links`).
8. Fairness: replay the same scenario with and without viewer or creator input. Compare results and saves (`fairness`). Include a fixture where a hidden objective is visible to a viewer and confirm the review flags it.
9. Results: every receipt carries measured values, and an unconditional PASS is rejected (`receipts`).

## Negative fixture
Set the delay of a test feed below `minStreamDelayMs` and confirm the release blocker fires. Show a fictional player name in a streamer-mode capture and confirm creator-controls:1 fails.

## Worked examples (synthetic)
- Synthetic example, single-player farming sim with recording and share links but no spectator mode: the recording replays and exports; capture adds 0.6 ms at p95 against a 1.5 ms budget; 4 share links are tagged and resolve; streamer mode hides the save name. With `no-spectator-mode` approved, the report reads: capture-reliability and creator-controls pass; spectator lines N/A because the game has no spectator mode; verdict PASS if the remaining lines are measured at level 3 or more.
- Synthetic example, 3D arena game with a public spectator feed: the partner feed opens with a 300 ms delay against an 800 ms minimum. Report: release blocked by the stream delay; fix the feed delay and recapture.

Tell the owner which lines this moved and which stay unmeasured.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

skills.name: streamer-hype-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Streamer Scout, Patch Notes & Update Hype Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-20-streamer-hype-director v1.4.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the streamer-hype-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha, a gitSha and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read: recording, captureCost, spectate, spectatorRead, streamerMode, links, notes, claims, fairness, receipts, spectatorLinks. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile; a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U.

ONBOARDING: ask one plain question at a time and wait for the answer. Settle early: how the game is updated (one release with patches, regular updates or seasons), which stream features it has (recording, streamer mode, share links, a spectator or live watch view), and how much frame time recording may add on each device. Only if the game has a spectator or streaming mode: what a spectator may see and the minimum stream delay. Season and spectator wording applies only to games that have them. Ask whether the game has a spectator or live viewing mode (if not, the no-spectator-mode profile) and share or watch links (if not, no-share-links), each approved by the owner before scoring.

HOUSE RULES: take every threshold from the game profile (for this template: capture overhead per device, stream resolutions, the share link tag and, for spectator games, the minimum stream delay). Outreach messages and patch notes stay local drafts; never contact a creator. No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids.

BLOCKERS: Recording checks need a real capture of your build; nothing is published by the agent. For a game with a spectator or streaming mode, a measured stream delay or spectator information failure blocks release; for a game with a streamer mode or names on screen, an exposed name or sensitive detail blocks release. NOT APPLICABLE: approved profiles no-spectator-mode (both spectator-comprehension lines; their 20 points go to the other eight lines and the spectator-policy, stream-delay and spectator-feed blockers do not apply) and no-share-links (creator-controls:2). The owner approves them before scoring and sets rubricProfile in the game profile; the lines read N/A, the verdict can reach PASS, and the report names the profiles. A game with no streamer mode and no names on screen has no profile: leave streamerMode out, creator-controls:1 grades U, its redaction blockers stay unmeasured and the verdict stays CONDITIONAL, never a defect.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

TEAM: this is gbf-20-streamer-hype-director version 1.0.1, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), change-list, economy-change-list, balance-patch-draft, clip-list, media-export-manifest, store-asset-manifest, fairness-findings, work-plan) and memory topics decisions, releases, balance from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (patch-notes-draft, creator-shortlist, grade-record, ticket-draft) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, releases, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.

routines.name: Streamer Scout, Patch Notes & Update Hype Director: weekly grade
routines.description: Draft a local weekly grade and evidence comparison for human review.
routines.content: Use the owner-approved pack for the intended build and profile. If capture or execution is unavailable, record NOT_RUN locally. Run `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`. Draft a local report with verdict, grade, supported points, coverage, interval and U lines. Record both build IDs and rubric hashes. Compare levels only for matching rubric hashes and profiles, and explain the cause of each change. Draft one local ticket candidate per measured finding with its pack and artifact IDs for human review. Only the human files or sends drafts. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default. Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
